exposure: Maternal perineal anatomy (perineal body and genital hiatus length)
finding: In nulliparous low-risk women, a larger infant head circumference at birth increases the likelihood of perineal trauma, although the effect is modest, while antenatal perineal body and genital hiatus measurements do not predict perineal trauma.
mod_finding: The study found no association between antenatal perineal body and genital hiatus measurements and perineal trauma, suggesting these factors do not necessitate alterations in mode of delivery.
